messages:
Maya R: quick thread — ran microbench across quant profiles; saw latency spike when KV hit ~70% on qwen-32B hybrid-fp8-int4-v2. attaching perf snippet.

Devon K: can you paste the exact cmd + profile? also which kernel selector was active?

Maya R: here's the run:
```bash
./profile_run --model qwen-32b --quant-profile hybrid-fp8-int4-v2 --batcher max_tokens=64 --kv-policy LRU --kvcopy on --kernel-selector default
```

Maya R: tail of p50/p95 logs:
```
step 120: tokens=2048 kv_hit=0.71 p50=43ms p95=310ms memcpy_gpu=24ms memcpy_cpu=3ms
step 121: tokens=2072 kv_hit=0.72 p50=45ms p95=560ms memcpy_gpu=180ms memcpy_cpu=3ms
```

infra-bot: background profiling job 2175012345-aux completed, rate-limited ops noted at 21:34 UTC

Liam C: hmm looks like a memcpy spike when kvcopy path kicks in and we hit mixed kernels. could be kernel adapter doing an extra host<->device copy for INT4 path. try `kvcopy=off` or `KERNEL_SELECTOR=force_fp8` to test.

Sienna (prod-reliability): we also saw a regression on canary last night — rolling to older kernel removed the spike. cc @Maya R @Devon K

Devon K: try with `--kvcopy=off` and also a run with `--quant-profile=int8-only` to isolate. also set `BATCHER_MAX_TOK_PER_REQ=32` to see batching effect. small batches reduce risk of crossing threshold.

Maya R: running quick variants now, will post results. thx

Maya R: quick update: `kvcopy=off` reduced p95 from 560ms -> 120ms. int8-only p95=100ms. suspected interplay between kvcopy + hybrid int4 kernels.

Liam C: interesting — sounds like kernel-selection fallback path isn't aligned with kvcopy optimization. filed a tiny task: KERNEL-4521 to check copy-insertion logic. ping me if you can reproduce with a minimal script.

Devon K: also add `--profiling=memcpy:gpu` and capture nvprof/torch.prof so we can see which op triggered the memcpy spike.

Maya R: will attach nvprof next. thanks all :thumbsup: 

Sienna (prod-reliability): good triage. if reproducible, we should add a canary test that toggles kvcopy across quant profile combos. otherwise might bite customers.
